alternatives.reason: A PROMOTED release is closed (ALREADY_PROMOTED). Re-opening it for a second target would let one approval cover two environments; the architecture requires a separate approval and separate config verification per environment.
Architecture §Release and plan v4.2 §Release: same digest is necessary, not sufficient — target, configuration hash, allowed environment delta, new revision and smoke are verified separately.
Same boundary as DR-008: P0 verifies what the operator deployed (scripts/record-promotion.sh) and keeps the control plane out of the cloud credential path.

P0 executes releases only for staging and an isolated prod-demo; development, testing, uat and other nodes are verified by evidence gates, production stays READ_ONLY/BLOCKED. Promotion must follow the topology order past evidence-only nodes.

architecture_impact: Adds the standard environment type prod-demo (topology). Releases execute only for staging and prod-demo; a release targeting any other type is GATE_BLOCKED by the environment gate with the P0 boundary spelled out.

POST /releases with source_release_id opens a promotion release: change lineage is copied from the source manifest (frozen by its receipt), the build (digest) is inherited and cannot be re-recorded (BUILD_INHERITED_FROM_SOURCE), the manifest carries a promotion block (source release, receipt id + hash, source revision, source environment config) and the environment delta between source and target config with its own hash.

Pre-deploy gates for a promotion: source_release (PROMOTED, receipt hash intact, same digest, not already promoted to this target), promotion_order (target is the next executable node after the source; evidence-only nodes in between are skipped and named), environment_delta (PASS, lists the fields the approval binds), change (live ledger must equal the frozen lineage, otherwise STALE naming the receipt), build (inherited), target_config_drift.

Deployment gates add new_revision: the observed revision must not be the source revision nor land on the source target — Cloud Run revisions belong to one service, a promotion creates a new revision on the target.

The Release Receipt of a promotion carries promotion, environment_delta and previous_receipt_id (staging receipt → prod-demo receipt chain) and adds receipt:<previous> to evidence_refs; release-receipt/v1 stays additive.

Frontend: a PROMOTED release with an executable next environment offers 'Promote'; the promotion detail shows source receipt, revision and the delta table, hides the build form, and the receipt shows the chain. Topology forms offer the prod-demo type.
cost_assumptions: No cloud resources in this slice. A real prod-demo promotion needs a second Cloud Run service (plan v4.2 budgets product + staging + prod-demo).
unknowns: No real prod-demo deployment has been recorded; every deployment in evidence is a declared fixture and scripts/record-promotion.sh remains UNVERIFIED against gcloud output.
Adding prod-demo to a topology after decisions were made is a material change and marks those decisions STALE by design; the demo script must add prod-demo before opening the change.
Cloud Run revision read-back inside the service is still not implemented; the operator script is the read-back path.
Same persistence and actor caveats as DR-005…DR-008.
acceptance_criteria: A PROMOTED staging release can be promoted to prod-demo with the same digest; the promotion is READY_FOR_APPROVAL without a build step and lists the environment delta.

Approval of the promotion binds a manifest that includes the delta hash; the staging revision name on prod-demo fails with new_revision; a new revision with the same digest and a passing smoke yields PROMOTED and a receipt whose previous_receipt_id is the staging receipt.
The same staging receipt cannot be promoted to prod-demo twice; promotion to production or to an evidence-only node is blocked; a non-PROMOTED source is refused.
A newer accepted candidate after the staging receipt makes the promotion STALE and blocks its deployment.
Consumer fixtures byte-identical after two consecutive browser runs.
